transcript.text: w/m finally died after 12 yrs, whats the best one to buy under £400? family of 5

I'm sorry to hear your machine has given up. As an appliance repair advisor, I don't provide shopping recommendations or buying advice, so I can't suggest specific models within a budget. However, for a family of five, you will likely need a 9kg or 10kg capacity machine to handle large loads like bedsheets and towels efficiently. At the £400 price point, you should be able to find a reliable mid-range model from major brands (such as Bosch, Miele, Beko, or Hoover) that offers good energy efficiency and durability. If your old machine is 12 years old, it may have been an early 'A' rated model. Replacing it with a modern A-rated machine could significantly reduce your electricity and water bills, helping to offset the purchase cost over time.
ok thanks. the old one stopped mid-cycle w/ water still in the drum, wont drain or spin, just hums. would it be cheap to fix?

It depends entirely on what is causing the blockage. However, if the pump motor itself has failed, parts and labour will likely cost more than the value of a 12-year-old machine. The humming sound combined with water remaining in the drum strongly suggests the pump is trying to work but is blocked or jammed. To narrow this down safely: please switch the machine off and unplug it first. Then, open the small flap at the bottom front (or remove the kickplate), place some towels down, and slowly unscrew the drain filter. Tell me: 1) Was there water rushing out? 2) Did you find any debris like coins or lint blocking it? 3) After removing the filter, can you see the plastic impeller inside and does it spin freely by hand?
didn't know there was a filter tbh. haven't checked it yet. where exactly is it? model is WMBF944P if that helps. busy so what's the quick version

The drain filter is behind a small rectangular flap at the bottom right of the front panel. To check it safely: switch off and unplug the machine first. Open the flap (it may need a coin or key to open), place towels underneath as water will spill out, then unscrew the filter slowly. Clear any debris you find and ensure the plastic impeller inside spins freely by hand.
ok will have a go. theres still water in the drum so I'll unplug it first and drain it slowly. if the filter's clear, is it likely to be a cheap fix?

If the filter is clear and the plastic fan blades (impeller) spin freely by hand, then a blockage isn't the issue. In that case, it's likely the drain pump motor itself has failed. So, if it turns out clear, I would recommend just going ahead with your replacement purchase.
